parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Good afternoon. As you know, the world is running out of fossil fuels, that is crude oil, coal and natural gas. As an alternative, certain plants are now being considered as biofuels, which are fuels made from organic plant material. These are possible sources of energy once the fossil fuels have gone forever.

Well, one such plant goes by the name of Jatropha. It was first a native of Central America, and it’s now found across the world. A few things that make this plant especially attractive is that it can survive in very poor quality and infertile soil, as it does, for example, alongside train tracks in India on the line between Mumbai and Delhi. And for up to three years, it’s resistant to drought. That’s right. It can do without rain for that long. And even if it’s not actually a plant that people can eat, it’s still worth having it on your land, as it prevents erosion. And we looked at the dangerous consequences of that in a previous lecture.

Furthermore, Jatropha seeds can be slowly distilled to produce diesel oil, and it’s this kind of fuel, of course, that’s of interest to scientists and power companies. After processing, the seeds can yield up to four times the oil that soybean can, and ten times the amount compared to corn, so you can see why it’s causing such interest. And not much is wasted in the processing procedure either. After the oil has been extracted from the seeds, the residue is processed into biomass, which can run power stations, which in turn can provide electricity for thousands of local homes. Also, whereas our fossil fuels cannot be replaced, the energy produced by biofuels such as Jatropha is renewable. It’s not going to run out because the plants just go on growing. There’s no doubt that it is a remarkable plant, and one that has been very beneficial to man.

In various African communities, it’s been used to operate water pumps and refrigerate medicine. It can be used to produce candles, or as a fencing plant to keep some animals enclosed, and some animals out. It can also treat a number of health problems, for example, the boiled leaves can do much to relieve the suffering of people with malaria and some Jatropha species have seeds which are used to treat digestion problems.

Anyway, that’s not what the European corporations who are buying vast amounts of land for Jatropha plantations are focusing on. They claim that people who are dependent on rural economies will benefit from growing Jatropha, and that it will help them bring an end to poverty by providing a long-term local industry. They also point out that few or no modifications would be necessary in modern diesel engines, since they were originally designed to run on biofuels such as peanut oil and ethanol anyway. Of course, when the plants are burnt, they release carbon dioxide, but they absorb great amounts when they’re growing, making them a considerably greener alternative to fossil fuels.

But not everyone shares the excitement over Jatropha, nor other biofuels. In Western Australia, Jatropha has in fact been banned since the seeds of some species are toxic, and it only takes three or four to kill a person and animals are also very vulnerable. Furthermore, skeptics also point out that as there are many species of Jatropha, its oil productivity is unreliable. Aside from this, critics of Jatropha and other biofuels claim that farmers now have a strong economic incentive to grow them rather than food crops. Poor countries would be particularly affected because they would have to rely on imported foods to survive, and people would end up having to pay greatly inflated prices for basic foods.

There’s also the concern over environmental damage. In order to provide land for palm oil or sugar cane plantations, for instance, companies are cutting down vast areas of rainforest which can never be replaced, and thus in turn results in the disappearance of wildlife which depended on that habitat. You can also imagine that such deforestation makes a considerable contribution to global warming. Furthermore, opponents also reject the idea that biofuels are a carbon neutral source of energy.

analyses.content: 录音中提到这种植物能在质量非常差且贫瘠的 soil（土壤）中生存。
A few things that make this plant especially attractive is that it can survive in very poor quality and infertile soil, as it does, for example, alongside train tracks in India...
不要听到 infertile（贫瘠的）就填进去，题目空格前已经有了 poor（差的），这里缺的是承载植物的名词。
And for up to three years, it’s resistant to drought. That’s right. It can do without rain for that long.
后面提到的 "do without rain"（没有雨也能活）是对 drought 的解释，不要填成 rain。
这种植物能够抵抗 drought（干旱/旱灾）长达三年。
And even if it’s not actually a plant that people can eat, it’s still worth having it on your land, as it prevents erosion.
题目中的 stop（停止/阻止）对应录音中的 prevents（防止）。
虽然不能吃，但这种植物值得种植，因为它能防止土地 erosion（侵蚀/水土流失）。
After processing, the seeds can yield up to four times the oil that soybean can, and ten times the amount compared to corn...
题目已经给出了 soybean，你需要捕捉“另一个”被比较的农作物。
演讲者对比了产油量，说它是大豆（soybean）的四倍，是 corn（玉米）的十倍。
It can be used to produce candles, or as a fencing plant to keep some animals enclosed...
题目中的 made into（被制成）对应录音中的 produce（生产/制造）。
在非洲社区，这种植物被用来制作 candles（蜡烛）。
录音明确提到，煮过的 leaves（叶子）可以极大地减轻疟疾患者的痛苦。
It can also treat a number of health problems, for example, the boiled leaves can do much to relieve the suffering of people with malaria...
不要填 seeds（种子），录音后半句才说 seeds 是用来治消化问题的，不要张冠李戴。
...and some Jatropha species have seeds which are used to treat digestion problems.
题目结构是 "problems with..."，所以听到 "treat digestion problems" 时，中间的修饰词就是答案。
紧接着上文，有些品种的种子被用来治疗 digestion（消化）问题。
Of course, when the plants are burnt, they release carbon dioxide, but they absorb great amounts [of carbon dioxide] when they’re growing...
题目中的 use up（用光/消耗）对应录音中的 absorb（吸收）。
虽然燃烧时会释放二氧化碳，但植物在生长过程中会吸收（use up）大量的 carbon dioxide（二氧化碳）。
...cutting down vast areas of rainforest which can never be replaced, and thus in turn results in the disappearance of wildlife which depended on that habitat.
题目中的 loss of（...的丧失）对应录音中的 disappearance of（...的消失）。
砍伐雨林导致了依赖该栖息地的 wildlife（野生动物）消失。
You can also imagine that such deforestation makes a considerable contribution to global warming.
注意区分因果，environmental damage 是大背景，wildlife 是具体的损失，而 global warming 是宏观的问题后果。
这种森林砍伐对 global warming（全球变暖）这一问题做出了相当大的“贡献”（负面影响）。
